Day 5 · Chapter 4: The Calendar (Part 2 of 2)

Day 5 Overview

Yesterday you filled your calendar with appointments and meetings. Today you'll make that calendar useful to other people — sharing it, comparing it against someone else's, and printing a hard copy — then wrap up the whole chapter with the Self-Assessment Quiz and Test.

Competencies Covered Today

  • Share your calendar
  • Print a calendar

Today's Tasks

  1. Sharing, Publishing & Creating More Calendars — read, then complete Hands-On OU4-D9 & D10
  2. Printing Calendars — read, then complete the Print Setup Hands-On
  3. Chapter 4 Self-Assessment Quiz and Test — these cover the whole chapter, Part 1 (Day 4) and Part 2 (today) together
Chapter 4 wraps up today

The Self-Assessment Quiz and Test at the bottom of this module test everything from both Day 4 and Day 5 — views, appointments, meetings, recurring appointments, sharing, and printing.

items.title: Sharing, Publishing & Creating More Calendars — Reading
items.body:
Day 5 · Chapter 4 Reading

Book pages: 77-80 · Chapter 4 · CBO Objective: Share your calendar

Sharing and Publishing Calendars

There are many ways to share a calendar, and this course covers two of them: sending a calendar via email and publishing it online. You can mark calendar items as private and then decide whether you want to share them. The default option is to not share them — when someone receives a calendar with items marked private, all they'll see on your calendar is Private Appointment. The sharing options available to you will vary depending on your Outlook configuration.

Creating More Calendars

You may want to create separate calendars for different areas of your work — for example, a dedicated calendar for a team project that you can share with just that team. The quickest way to create one is to right-click an existing calendar in the Folder pane and choose New Calendar.

Displaying Multiple Calendars

Once you have more than one calendar, they all show up in a list under My Calendars in the Navigation pane. You can switch back and forth between them side by side, or overlay them so they display on one shared set of dates and times — handy for checking a coworker's schedule against your own to find a good meeting time. Outlook assigns each calendar its own color so you can tell them apart; in Overlay mode, whichever calendar is on top stays fully readable while the other shows through in fainter text.

{{img:pg 78.png|Textbook page 78 — the right-click New Calendar menu, and the Displaying Multiple Calendars section showing two calendars side by side and overlaid}}

Copying Calendar Items

The simplest way to copy an item from one calendar to another is to view them side by side and drag the event onto the same time on the other calendar — this is usually easiest in Month view.

Sending a Calendar via Email

If you want your contacts to know when you're available and when you're busy, you can share your calendar with them by email. They'll be able to see any updates you make as meetings and appointments are added or changed. Recipients can choose to view the calendar right in the email message, or open it as its own Outlook calendar and position it side by side with theirs or in Overlay mode.

Marking Items as Private

Any item on your calendar — appointments and meetings alike — can be marked private. When you share your calendar with someone, you decide whether to share those private items or keep them hidden. A small padlock appears at the bottom right of a private appointment's peek card, and the shortcut menu on any calendar item includes a Private option.

Sending Options

The shortcut menu on any calendar lets you create an email with that calendar attached. In the Send a Calendar via Email window, you can choose a date range (like the whole calendar or just the next 30 days), and a Detail level — Availability only (just Free/Busy/Tentative/Out of Office), Limited details (availability plus the subjects of calendar items), or Full details (availability and the full details of every item).

{{img:pg 80.png|Textbook page 80 — the Send a Calendar via Email window with its Date Range and Detail drop-downs, and the start of the Publishing a Calendar Online section}}

Publishing a Calendar Online

If you want someone to see your calendar without you having to email it, you can publish it online first and then share it — a more dynamic option, since the person you share it with sees changes as you make them. This is a good fit for calendars tracking a group project. You'll typically publish to whatever online service you use for email, such as Outlook.com.

items.title: Hands-On OU4-D9 & D10: Compare & Share Calendars
items.description:
Book pages: 79-81 · Develop Your Skills OU4-D9 & OU4-D10

Hands-On OU4-D9 & D10: Compare & Share Calendars

Hands-On Exercise

Part 1 — OU4-D9: Display Multiple Calendars (Overlay)

  1. In the Folder pane, check the box next to a second calendar — use US Holidays or Birthday calendar if you have one; if not, right-click your calendar and choose New Calendar first to create a second one to compare against.
  2. Choose View → More Commands (…) → Overlay.
  3. Notice both calendars now share one set of dates, with the second calendar's items shown in fainter text. Switch back to Side-by-Side mode and compare the two views.

Part 2 — OU4-D10: Share a Calendar via Email

  1. Right-click your Calendar's title bar and choose Share → E-mail Calendar.
  2. Set the Date Range to Next 30 Days and the Detail level to Limited details. Click OK.
  3. Required: address the message to a classmate or your instructor, using their real VACE email address.
  4. Click Send.
What to submit

Two screenshots: (1) your calendar in Overlay mode with both calendars' items visible; (2) the sent calendar-sharing email showing your recipient and the attached calendar.

criteria.description: Screenshot shows the calendar in Overlay mode with items from both calendars visible

ratings.description: Full Credit — Overlay mode is clearly shown with both calendars' items
Partial Credit — a calendar is shown but Overlay mode / the second calendar isn't clearly visible
No Credit — missing or unrelated screenshot

criteria.description: Screenshot shows the sent calendar-sharing email with a real recipient

ratings.description: Full Credit — the sent email is shown with a recipient address and the calendar attached/embedded
Partial Credit — an email is shown but the recipient or attached calendar isn't clearly visible
No Credit — missing or unrelated screenshot

items.title: Printing Calendars — Reading
items.body:
Day 5 · Chapter 4 Reading

Book pages: 81-82 · Chapter 4 · CBO Objective: Print a calendar

Printing Calendars

Sometimes it's handy to have a hard copy of your calendar — if you're out on the road and leaving the computer behind, you can print your appointments to take with you. You can choose to print the Day, Week, or Month view, then choose which dates to include.

{{img:pg 82.png|Textbook page 82 — the calendar Print dialog, showing print style options (Monthly, Tri-fold, Calendar Details), a Page Setup button, print range, a specific date range, and the option to hide the details of private appointments}}

The Print dialog lets you pick which calendar to print, a print style (Monthly Style, Tri-fold Style, Calendar Details Style, or a style you define yourself), and a specific date range to include. Page Setup opens more detailed settings, like limiting the printout to workdays only or adding headers and footers. And if some of your appointments are marked private, you can choose whether to hide their details on the printed copy.

items.title: Hands-On: Print Setup
items.description:
Book page: 81-82

Hands-On: Print Setup

Hands-On Exercise
  1. Click File → Print.
  2. Under Settings, choose the Monthly Style print style.
  3. Set the print range to the current month (or any date range of your choosing).
  4. Take a screenshot of the Print screen showing your chosen style and date range — you do not need to actually print anything.
What to submit

One screenshot of the Print screen with the Monthly Style and your chosen date range visible.

criteria.description: Screenshot shows the Print screen with a chosen print style and date range

ratings.description: Full Credit — the print style and date range are both clearly visible
Partial Credit — the Print screen is shown but the style or date range isn't clearly visible
No Credit — missing or unrelated screenshot

questions.question_text: Why are some days and times grayed out in the calendar?

answers.text: They're outside the designated work hours.

questions.question_text: Why is the Weather bar included on the Outlook calendar?

answers.text: It allows Outlook to alert you to when adverse weather conditions are affecting email delivery.

answers.text: Change her working times to match her client's.
Add the client's time zone to her calendar.
Assign the client a task for each meeting and phone call.

What happened to the 5-minute reminder for the next occurrence?
